description: Count orders whose placement timestamp falls in the window, excluding orders placed exactly at either endpoint.

c.request: Looking at orders placed in the period between '2013-10-25 17:40:25' and '2017-05-24 19:26:44' (compare `date_order_placed` as text), count each customer gender's orders, using only orders whose customer exists. Which genders have an order count above the average across genders? Show each such gender, its order count, and how far that count is above the average. Count orders whose placement timestamp falls in the window, excluding orders placed exactly at either endpoint.
c.sql: WITH gender_counts AS (SELECT c.gender, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM Orders AS o JOIN Customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE CAST(o.date_order_placed AS TEXT) > '2013-10-25 17:40:25' AND CAST(o.date_order_placed AS TEXT) < '2017-05-24 19:26:44' GROUP BY c.gender) SELECT gender, order_count, order_count - (SELECT AVG(order_count) FROM gender_counts) AS above_average FROM gender_counts WHERE order_count > (SELECT AVG(order_count) FROM gender_counts);

a.request: Take orders placed strictly after '2013-10-25 17:40:25' and strictly before '2017-05-24 19:26:44', both endpoints excluded, comparing `date_order_placed` as text. Keep only orders whose customer exists and count them by the customer's `gender`. Which genders have an order count above the average of these per-gender counts? Show each such gender, its order count, and how far that count is above the average.
a.sql: WITH gender_counts AS (SELECT c.gender, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM Orders AS o JOIN Customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE CAST(o.date_order_placed AS TEXT) > '2013-10-25 17:40:25' AND CAST(o.date_order_placed AS TEXT) < '2017-05-24 19:26:44' GROUP BY c.gender), average_count AS (SELECT AVG(order_count) AS avg_order_count FROM gender_counts) SELECT gc.gender, gc.order_count, gc.order_count - ac.avg_order_count AS above_average FROM gender_counts AS gc CROSS JOIN average_count AS ac WHERE gc.order_count > ac.avg_order_count

b.request: For orders with an existing customer and a `date_order_placed` text value strictly greater than '2013-10-25 17:40:25' and strictly less than '2017-05-24 19:26:44', count orders by customer gender and report each gender whose count exceeds the average order count across genders, along with its count and the amount above that average.
b.sql: WITH gender_counts AS (SELECT c.gender, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM Orders AS o JOIN Customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.date_order_placed > '2013-10-25 17:40:25' AND o.date_order_placed < '2017-05-24 19:26:44' GROUP BY c.gender), gender_average AS (SELECT AVG(order_count) AS average_order_count FROM gender_counts) SELECT gc.gender, gc.order_count, gc.order_count - ga.average_order_count AS amount_above_average FROM gender_counts AS gc CROSS JOIN gender_average AS ga WHERE gc.order_count > ga.average_order_count

d.request: For orders with a matching customer and a `date_order_placed` text value strictly between '2013-10-25 17:40:25' and '2017-05-24 19:26:44', count orders by customer gender and return each gender whose count exceeds the average count across genders, along with its order count and the amount above that average.
d.sql: WITH gender_counts AS (SELECT c.gender, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM Orders AS o JOIN Customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE CAST(o.date_order_placed AS TEXT) > '2013-10-25 17:40:25' AND CAST(o.date_order_placed AS TEXT) < '2017-05-24 19:26:44' GROUP BY c.gender), gender_average AS (SELECT AVG(order_count) AS average_count FROM gender_counts) SELECT gc.gender, gc.order_count, gc.order_count - ga.average_count AS amount_above_average FROM gender_counts AS gc CROSS JOIN gender_average AS ga WHERE gc.order_count > ga.average_count
